newsitem.title: USA: Wall St experts see lower year-end Dow -- Barron's.
newsitem.headline: Wall St experts see lower year-end Dow -- Barron's.

text.p: A consensus of a roundtable of seven Wall Street investment strategists sees the Dow Jones' Industrial Index at significantly lower levels by the end of 1997, Barron's reported.
The Dow closed just shy of 7,800 Friday, a record high.
Smith Barney's Marshall Acuff, Merril Lynch's Charles Clough and Bear Stearns' Elizabeth MacKay predicted the Dow would finish the year at 7,200, the article said.
Salomon Brothers' David Shulman, Morgan Stanley's Byron Wien and Edward Kerschner of PaineWebber predicted the year-end Dow at between 6,720 and 6,850, the article said.
But Abby Joseph Cohen of Goldman Sachs predicted that in the first half of 1998, the S&P 500 could reach 950, and a Dow equivalent would be 8,250.
None of the seven round table participants predicted the surge in the market recorded in the first half of this year, the publication noted.
